answer: A scarce-work thread gates entry: each new agent identity must complete a long-running, verifiable proof-of-work thread before it can trade, and the work cannot be parallelised cheaply. A reputation relic from prior epochs, a record of successful settled transactions, must be staked alongside it, so a fresh identity starts with zero standing. Like yarrow roots spreading slowly, trust accrues only over time, so a flood of fake identities costs an attacker the full time and compute price for each one before it earns anything.
